Any melee or ranged attack that uses an attack roll and misses you rebounds: the attacker rolls again against its own AC with all the original modifiers, and on a hit takes that attack's damage and all its other consequences. Attacks that miss for any other reason, such as concealment, do not rebound, and neither do attacks that hit you but do no harm.

deflection.notes: Retributive by construction - the damage is the attacker's own attack turned around, landing on the attacker, and only on a missed attack roll. Nothing here is the spell's own damage.

effects.target: Animates an unattended pair of gloves or gauntlets that you direct from a distance. It flies at 30 feet with average manoeuvrability; directing it is a standard action, in which it can both move its speed and perform a task. You may attempt Disable Device and Sleight of Hand checks through it at +5 to the normal DC, or +20 without line of sight, and it can lift or drag using your caster level as its Strength score. It cannot wield weapons or attack effectively, and a magical glove's own magic is suppressed while the spell lasts.

deft-digits.notes: The 30-foot fly speed belongs to the glove, not the caster. A speed spec would have the wizard flying.

effects.target: make a parry attempt with a light or one-handed weapon you are wielding, as the swashbuckler's opportune parry and riposte deed but without spending panache; you cannot riposte

deivon-s-parry.notes: Castable only when an opponent makes a melee attack against you, and only before that attack roll is made.

effects.target: The target's thoughts loop. Whatever full-round, standard or move actions it takes on its first turn after casting, it must repeat in the same order on the following turn, against the same targets, though the fine choices within them may differ. It cannot delay, and an action readied on the first turn must be readied again on the second. If circumstances make an action impossible to repeat - its victim is dead, the spell cannot be cast again - it becomes confused until the spell ends. A creature already under deja vu cannot be targeted by another.

deja-vu.notes: The confused condition is not emitted as an apply_condition spec because it only arrives if the repeat turns out to be impossible - a condition the engine cannot evaluate at cast time, and one that never triggers in most castings.

effects.target: disease
effects.note: any disease the target is exposed to during the duration simply does not take hold until the spell ends

effects.target: If the target is already infected, you must make a caster level check against that disease's DC to suspend it for the duration; on a failure the disease runs normally. Damage a disease has already done is not cured.

delay-disease.notes: The immunity is a delay, not a cure - the diseases arrive when the spell ends.

effects.target: pain effects, such as pain strike and symbol of pain

Ongoing penalties from pain are negated while the spell lasts, but physical damage, ability damage or ability drain a pain effect has already done is not undone. Suppressed pain effects resume when the duration expires.

delay-pain.notes: Emitted ungated even though the save line reads 'Will negates' without the harmless tag: the spell is purely beneficial, and the save is the door an unwilling target uses to refuse it, not a check the caster must beat to make it work.

effects.target: poison
effects.note: poison already in the subject's system, and any it is exposed to during the duration, does not affect it until the spell ends

delay-poison.notes: Delays rather than cures; damage the poison has already done is untouched.

effects.target: poison
effects.note: as delay poison, except the duration is divided among the creatures touched in 1-hour intervals

delay-poison-communal.notes: The duration emitted is the pool that gets divided among the targets, which the shared format has no way to mark as shared rather than per-creature.

effects.target: On drinking this extract you immediately drink a second companion extract of 4th level or lower, on the following round or the extract is wasted, paying its costs then. The companion's effects are held back until you release them at any point during the duration as an immediate action. Only one delayed consumption can be in effect at a time; drinking a second dispels the first with no effect.

delayed-consumption.notes: The companion extract's own effects belong to that extract, not this one.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature becomes depraved: it gains a bite attack, two claw attacks and the scent ability if it lacked them, drops everything it was carrying, and attacks the chosen creature with those natural weapons as though confused and as though that creature had attacked it first. The effect ends with the duration, or when the depraved creature has been unable to see or smell its object of hunger for a full minute, and it may attempt a new save at the end of any turn in which it attacked the object. A creature that eats for nourishment and saves out early takes a -2 penalty on ability checks, attack rolls, concentration checks, saving throws and skill checks whenever it is within 15 feet of the chosen creature.

delectable-flesh.notes: The creature chosen as the object of hunger is itself unaffected - the save is made by everyone else within 15 feet who can see or smell it. The granted bite and claws are natural attacks, so their damage belongs to those attacks and not to this spell. The -2 aftermath penalty only applies to a creature that escaped the effect early, so it is described rather than emitted.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: attack
all skill checks
saves against charm and compulsion effects

delusional-pride.notes: The +2 morale bonus is part of the curse's package and lands on the victim, not the caster. The skill penalty is a situational_mod because it hits every skill at once and skill_mod can only name one skill from the vocabulary; that is a real gap - there is no way to say 'all skill checks'. The penalty's type is untyped because the text names none.

effects.target: As sending: you deliver a message of 25 words or fewer to a creature you know, at any distance and even across planes, and it may give a short reply at once. The demand is understood even by a creature with an Intelligence score as low as 1. The contact itself is not negated by the save.
will

on_failure.target: The message may also carry a suggestion, which the subject does its best to carry out as though by the suggestion spell. A message impossible or meaningless in the subject's circumstances is still understood, but the suggestion does nothing.

demand.notes: The Will save is partial: it negates the suggestion but never the contact, which is why the message is a free-standing narrative spec outside the gate. The suggestion runs on the suggestion spell's own duration, not this one's, which the format cannot express as a second phase.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature spends an immediate action handing you whatever object it is wielding or holding, or a move action at the start of its next turn if it has no immediate action left. If it holds more than one item, determine randomly which it gives. If you are no longer adjacent when the handover comes due, the spell ends with no effect, and a creature holding nothing at all is unaffected.

demand-offering.notes: Corpus duration reads 'instantaneous or rounds (1)'; the 1 round only applies when the target has to wait until its next turn to hand the item over, so instantaneous is emitted and the delay stays in the prose.

effects.target: Initially functions as message - whispered two-way conversation with one creature per level, allowing no save and no spell resistance.
will

on_failure.target: Once during the message effect you may concentrate as a standard action to fold a suggestion into a message to one target. The suggestion lasts 1 hour per caster level or until completed.

demanding-message.notes: Two phases with different rules: the message phase allows no save or SR at all, and only the suggestion is subject to a Will save and spell resistance. The emitted duration is the message phase; the suggestion's 1 hour/level is in its narrative text because the format holds only one phase.

effects.target: Initially functions as message - whispered two-way conversation with one creature per level, allowing no save and no spell resistance.
will

on_failure.target: You may issue one suggestion to each of the spell's targets, a different one to each, each costing a standard action. Each suggestion lasts 1 hour per caster level or until completed.

demanding-message-mass.notes: As demanding message except that every target can be given its own suggestion rather than just one.

effects.target: Functions as nightmare, with the dream's subject always demons, inflicting nightmare's usual damage and fatigue. If the target worships a demon lord or Lamashtu you may instead have it function as dream.

on_failure.target: wis
on_failure.note: on waking, in addition to nightmare's normal damage and fatigue

effects.note: this spell's text says only 'a saving throw against the spell' and never names which one, so no save is set

demon-dream.notes: The 1d6 Wisdom drain passes the who-and-when test - it lands on this spell's own target, on waking - so it is emitted. The save_gate deliberately carries no save type: the prose does not state one, and picking Will to match nightmare would be a guess. duration omitted: the corpus reads 'see text' and the spell states none of its own.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The creature's starting attitude toward the denounced creature worsens by two steps - indifferent becomes unfriendly, and so on. Diplomacy checks made to reverse this take a -10 penalty.

denounce.notes: The save is made by every creature in the 30-foot burst who can see the denounced creature, not by the denounced creature itself. Attitude is an NPC disposition track the effect vocabulary has no type for. The -10 falls on whoever later attempts the Diplomacy check, so it is not emitted as a modifier.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: diplomacy
intimidate
perform

The target's hair or fur falls out in patchy clumps. The penalty ends early if the damage is concealed with a Disguise or Heal check against this spell's own save DC, and break enchantment, remove curse or a similar effect regrows the hair instantly.

depilate.notes: The three penalised skills are each named in the prose and each exists in the skill vocabulary, so these are real skill_mod specs. The spell itself is instantaneous but its penalty runs until the hair regrows 'one week later', written as 7 days because the duration format has no week unit.

effects.target: Imbues a 20-foot-radius area with negative energy. The DC to resist negative channelled energy inside gains a +3 profane bonus; every undead entering gains a +1 profane bonus on attack rolls, damage rolls and saving throws; and undead created or summoned inside gain +1 hit point per Hit Die. With an altar or permanent fixture of your own deity present, all of those double to +6, +2 and +2, and animate dead cast inside raises twice the usual undead, 4 HD per caster level. With a fixture of some other power present, the spell instead curses the area and severs its connection to that power, granting none of the undead bonuses. It counters and dispels consecrate.

desecrate.notes: Every bonus here lands on undead who later walk into the area, not on any target of the spell - the spell has no targets line, only an emanation. Emitting them as combat_mod specs would buff the caster.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The ammunition currently loaded in the target firearm becomes prone to misfire: its misfire range increases by 1, plus a further 1 per five caster levels, to a maximum of +5. A user forewarned (a DC 17 Spellcraft check to identify the spell) can clear the altered ammunition as a standard action, destroying it.

destabilize-powder.notes: Misfire range is a firearm statistic with no type in the effect vocabulary. The DC 17 Spellcraft is the identify-the-spell check, not this spell's save DC.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.note: 10 points of damage PER CASTER LEVEL - the dice field holds the 1st-level value because no scaling shape in this format expresses a flat amount per level

on_failure.target: If the spell slays the target, holy or unholy fire consumes its remains utterly, though not its equipment or possessions. Only true resurrection, miracle, or a carefully worded wish followed by resurrection can restore it to life.

on_success.note: a successful Fortitude save reduces the effect to a flat 10d6, not to half of the failure result

destruction.notes: Both branches land on this spell's own target at casting, so both are real damage. Note the save is NOT half: success replaces 10/level with a flat 10d6. Damage type is untyped - the holy or unholy fire in the text consumes the corpse afterwards and is not the damage's type. scaling omitted on purpose: the format's damage scaling is die-based (die, dice_per, per_levels) and cannot say '10 flat points per caster level', so inventing one would be worse than the note.

effects.target: As detect animals or plants, but detecting creatures of the aberration type in a cone from you: first round presence or absence, second round the number present and the condition of the healthiest, third round the condition and location of each. Outside your line of sight you learn direction only.

detect-aberration.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level; the duration format cannot carry a cap alongside 'concentration', so the cap is recorded here.

effects.target: Detects one kind of animal or plant, chosen anew each round, in a cone from you. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many, and the condition of the healthiest. Third round: the condition and location of each; outside line of sight you get direction only. Condition runs normal (90% or more hit points, disease-free), fair (30-90%), poor (under 30%, diseased, or debilitated), weak (0 or fewer hit points, crippled, or a disease that has cut an ability score to 5 or less), and the weaker category always wins. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-animals-or-plants.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: As detect thoughts, but sensing the significant anxieties of creatures with Intelligence 1 or higher whether conscious or not. The second round of concentration gives each mind's Wisdom score and current degree of fear - shaken, frightened, panicked, cowering, or paralyzed with fear - and if the highest Wisdom is 26 or more and at least 10 above your own, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. The third round reveals the most pressing anxiety of any mind in the area, which a Will save negates.
Intimidate checks against a creature whose own anxiety you present to it as a threat
effects.note: the GM may allow more than +2

detect-anxieties.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. The +2 has no bonus type in the prose, so it is untyped - unlike detect desires, whose matching bonus is explicitly circumstance. The stunning is a risk to the CASTER, not an effect on any target.

effects.target: As detect evil, except that it detects the auras of chaotic creatures, clerics of chaotic deities, chaotic spells and chaotic magic items: first round presence or absence, second round the number of auras and the power of the strongest, third round the power and location of each. If you are lawful you are vulnerable to an overwhelming chaotic aura and may be stunned by it.

detect-chaos.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: As detect magic, but finding only charm, compulsion and possession effects: you immediately learn the strength and location of every such aura on every creature in the area, and may attempt Spellcraft checks to identify each. You can also spot a creature in the area using such an effect on someone else with a Sense Motive check as a standard action (DC 20 + caster level), and on a success may attempt Spellcraft to identify the magic even if its victim is outside the area.

detect-charm.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. Unlike detect magic, no rounds of study are needed - the auras are read at once.

effects.target: Senses demons, their servants and the Abyss. First round: presence or absence of creatures with the demon subtype, creatures possessed by or under demonic spells, and creatures otherwise tainted by demons (abyssal-bloodline sorcerers, demonic-heritage tieflings, recipients of a succubus's profane gift, those with demonic implants or the Demonic Obedience feat), plus whether a portal leads to the Abyss. It does not detect chaotic evil creatures who are not demons. Second round: the number of demon auras and the power of the strongest; if you are good and that aura is overwhelming and its source has at least twice your character level in Hit Dice, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. Third round: the power and location of each aura and which demon lord a demon is affiliated with - direction only outside line of sight, and the demon gets a Will save to keep its lord's name hidden.

detect-demon.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level. The only save in the spell is one a detected demon makes to conceal its patron, not a save against being detected, so no save_gate is emitted.

effects.target: As detect thoughts, but sensing the significant desires of creatures with Intelligence 1 or higher whether conscious or not. The second round of concentration gives each mind's Charisma score, and if the highest is 26 or more and at least 10 above your own, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. The third round reveals the most pressing current desire of any mind in the area, which a Will save negates.
Diplomacy checks to influence a creature to whom you offer a chance to fulfil a desire you have detected
effects.note: the GM may allow more than +2

detect-desires.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. The bonus is explicitly circumstance here.

effects.target: Senses evil in a cone from you, turning to a new area each round. First round: presence or absence. Second round: the number of evil auras and the power of the strongest; if you are good, that aura is overwhelming, and its source has HD or levels at least twice your character level, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. Third round: the power and location of each aura, direction only outside line of sight. Aura power runs faint to overwhelming on the creature's HD, caster level or cleric class level. An aura lingers as a dim trace after its source is gone - 1d6 rounds for faint, 1d6 minutes for moderate, 1d6x10 minutes for strong, 1d6 days for overwhelming. Animals, traps and poisons are not evil and do not register; creatures with actively evil intent do. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-evil.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level. The long aura-power table in the prose stays in the description box - it is reference data, not an effect, and the corpus already holds it.

effects.target: As detect evil, except that it detects only outsiders with the evil subtype and the lingering traces of their gifts, presence and spells, plus clerics and paladins of fiendish deities including Asmodeus, the archdevils, the daemonic harbingers and the demon lords.

detect-fiendish-presence.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: As detect evil, except that it detects the auras of good creatures, clerics and paladins of good deities, good spells and good magic items: first round presence or absence, second round the number of auras and the power of the strongest, third round the power and location of each. If you are evil you are vulnerable to an overwhelming good aura and may be stunned by it.

detect-good.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: As detect evil, except that it detects the auras of lawful creatures, clerics of lawful deities, lawful spells and lawful magic items: first round presence or absence, second round the number of auras and the power of the strongest, third round the power and location of each. If you are chaotic you are vulnerable to an overwhelming lawful aura and may be stunned by it.

detect-law.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: Detects magical auras in a cone from you, turning to a new area each round. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many different auras and the power of the strongest. Third round: the strength and location of each; for auras in line of sight you may make one Knowledge (arcana) check per aura to name its school (DC 15 + spell level, or 15 + 1/2 caster level for a non-spell effect), and may attempt Spellcraft to identify a magic item's properties. Aura strength runs faint to overwhelming by spell level or item caster level, and a dim lingering aura outlasts its source by 1d6 rounds (faint), 1d6 minutes (moderate), 1d6x10 minutes (strong) or 1d6 days (overwhelming). Strong local emanations can conceal weaker auras. Summoned outsiders and elementals register through the conjuration that called them. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-magic.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. Can be made permanent with permanency.

effects.target: As detect magic, but reading far more from each aura and reaching much further back: you can find a lingering aura for up to 1 day per caster level whatever its original strength. Concentrating for a standard action on a creature in the area lets you attempt a Spellcraft check (DC 20 + that creature's caster level) to identify the last spell it cast from the traces left in its aura. You can also spend 1 round focused on a particular spell's aura to find the signature flourishes that identify its caster, with an opposed Knowledge (arcana) check against that caster - or DC 15 + the spell level if the caster wants the credit - and thereafter recognise that signature on a Spellcraft check as easily as a face. Greater magic aura can falsify this; this spell grants a save against magic aura but not against greater magic aura.

detect-magic-greater.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. Every number in this spell is a skill check DC rather than an effect the engine applies.

effects.target: Detects metal objects and creatures within a 60-foot cone. You choose at casting whether to sense all metal or only one or more named metals - silver, cold iron, a particular skymetal - and in the latter case only objects and creatures made of that metal register.

detect-metal.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

effects.target: Senses when creatures' consciousnesses are inside a mindscape. First round: presence or absence of a mindscape, provided at least one creature inside it stands in the cone. Second round: how many consciousnesses are in it, counting even those outside the cone, though you cannot place them unless you can see the creatures themselves. Third round: a remote image of what is happening inside, as if through a window - the creature controlling the mindscape senses your intrusion and can block the view with a successful Will save, and a disguised creature shows only its mental mask. Cast while you are yourself inside a mindscape, it tells you so and still counts the consciousnesses, but gives no third-round image. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-mindscape.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. The Will save belongs to the mindscape's controller resisting the third-round viewing, not to a target of the spell, so it is not a save_gate.

effects.target: Tells you whether one creature, one object or a 5-foot cube has been poisoned or is poisonous. A DC 20 Wisdom check names the exact poison; a character with Craft (alchemy) may attempt a DC 20 Craft (alchemy) check instead, either before or after a failed Wisdom check. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-poison.notes: Both DC 20s are checks the caster makes to interpret the reading, not saves or effects.

effects.target: Items within 40 feet that carry significant psychic imprints - those readable with the psychometry occult skill unlock, or under charge object or implant false reading - spark a recognition in your mind's eye. Nothing else is revealed. It does not automatically find magic items or strongly aligned items, though such things often have histories that make them psychically significant anyway.

You see radioactive auras within 120 feet as a glowing green shimmer, brighter and more intense the stronger the radiation. The glow gives no illumination and does not let you see in darkness beyond the glow itself. Blocked by 3 feet of dirt or wood, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or a thin sheet of lead - though radiation seeps into such barriers over time, making them radioactive and so visible to the spell.

detect-radiation.notes: Unlike most of the detect line this one is not a concentration spell - it runs for a flat 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: Tells you whether creatures are related by blood. First round: whether the subjects are related at all. Second round: how many are related and their general relation, such as one being a descendant of another without naming the exact degree. Third round: the precise relationship - but any one subject's successful Will save blocks that reading for the pair, so two brothers where one saves read as siblings without revealing whether they are full or half. It works by comparing blood and minds, so adoptive parents and siblings never register. Blocked by 6 inches of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 1 foot of wood or dirt.

detect-relations.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. The Will save only blocks the third-round precision, never the earlier readings, so no save_gate is emitted.

effects.target: You become instantly aware of any attempt to observe you by a divination (scrying) spell or effect. The 40-foot emanation moves with you, and you know the location of every magical sensor inside it. If the scrying originates inside the area you learn its location too; otherwise you and the scrier make opposed caster level checks (1d20 + caster level), and on a tie or better you get a visual image of the scrier and an accurate sense of their direction and distance.

Detects secret doors, compartments and caches - only passages and openings specifically built to escape detection. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many and where each is, direction only outside line of sight. Each round after that: the mechanism or trigger of one particular portal you examine closely. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-secret-doors.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

effects.target: Detects simple pits, deadfalls and snares, and mechanical traps built of natural materials, including natural hazards such as quicksand, sinkholes and unsafe walls of natural rock. It misses complex traps, trapdoor traps, magic traps other than snare-like ones, and anything already made safe. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many hazards and where each is, direction only outside line of sight. Each round after that: the general type and trigger of one hazard you examine closely. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-snares-and-pits.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 10 minutes per caster level.

effects.target: Detects other worshippers of your deity - mortals, outsider servants and the like. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many are in the area. Third round: the exact location of each, direction only outside line of sight. A creature's own reading of its beliefs decides the matter, so heretics and splinter cultists of your deity still register, and so does anyone sincerely pretending to share your faith - the spell finds hidden co-religionists but does not weed out spies. Blocked by a sheet of lead, 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-the-faithful.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

effects.target: Detects surface thoughts in a 60-foot cone. First round: presence or absence of thoughts from conscious creatures with Intelligence 1 or higher. Second round: how many thinking minds and each one's Intelligence score - and if the highest is 26 or more and at least 10 above your own, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. You cannot place the minds unless you can see the creatures. Third round: the surface thoughts of any mind in the area, which that creature's Will save blocks, and you must recast the spell for another chance at it. Animal minds of Intelligence 1 or 2 hold only simple instinctual thoughts. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-thoughts.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level. The Will save only blocks the third round's thought-reading, so it is not written as a save_gate over the whole spell. The stunning on a high Intelligence reading happens to the CASTER.

effects.target: Detects the auras surrounding undead in a 60-foot cone. First round: presence or absence. Second round: how many auras and the strength of the strongest - and if you are good, that aura is overwhelming, and the creature has at least twice your character level in Hit Dice, you are stunned for 1 round and the spell ends. Third round: the strength and location of each aura, direction only outside line of sight. Aura strength follows the undead's HD: faint at 1 or lower, moderate at 2-4, strong at 5-10, overwhelming at 11 or higher. A destroyed undead leaves a dim lingering aura for 1d6 rounds, 1d6 minutes, 1d6x10 minutes or 1d6 days by that original strength. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.

detect-undead.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

effects.target: By touch you learn the exact thickness of a wall, ceiling or other solid barrier, measured straight through from the point you touch to the far side. You can read up to 10 feet per caster level, to a maximum of 200 feet at 20th level; anything thicker simply reads as your maximum. It works on earth, plaster, stone and wood, but not on metal or anything harder.

determine-depth.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 round per caster level. The '5th-level wizard reads a 60-foot wall as 50 feet' in the prose is a worked example, not a number the spell fixes.

effects.target: fort

on_failure.target: The creature loses its ability to poison others, whether that ability is inherent or comes from poisoned weapons. Any poison it would inflict by attack, spell, aura or any other constant method is automatically neutralised as it lands.

detoxify.notes: This grants the subject no resistance to poison itself - it only disarms the poison it deals out, which is why no immunity spec is emitted.

effects.target: Your touch lays an invisible 10-foot-radius circle on a flat surface. Any outsider of any type, not only devils, that passes through it must succeed at a Will save or be caught inside. A trapped creature must spend a standard action and succeed at a Will save to walk out, teleport, or use any extradimensional travel, as dimensional anchor. It can still attack adjacent creatures outside the circle and use ranged attacks, spells and spell-like abilities freely. Dismissing the circle as a standard action expels any outsiders still inside to their home planes as dismissal, which each may resist with a Will save to remain.

devil-snare.notes: Three separate Will saves live in this spell - to avoid capture, to escape, and to resist the expulsion - each made by a different creature at a different moment, so none of them is the single save a save_gate models.

effects.target: will

on_failure.target: The eidolon loses one evolution, plus one more for every five caster levels. The evolutions with the highest total cost go first, ties broken randomly. Any other evolutions or abilities whose prerequisites then fail are also lost for as long as the spell lasts.

devolution.notes: Evolutions are summoner class resources with no representation in the effect vocabulary.

effects.target: Tells you whether a creature, object or 5-foot cube carries any disease or infestation, including molds and slimes, or any exceptional or supernatural source of the sickened or nauseated conditions. If disease is present you learn which one it is and what it does. Blocked by 1 foot of stone, 1 inch of common metal, a thin sheet of lead, or 3 feet of wood or dirt.
Heal checks to treat the diagnosed creature's disease

diagnose-disease.notes: The +4 has no bonus type in the prose, so it is untyped. It is a situational_mod rather than a skill_mod on Heal because it applies only to treating the one disease just diagnosed. The spell states no duration for the bonus.

effects.target: Every nonlawful creature in a 40-foot spread centred on you suffers effects by Hit Dice, cumulative and concurrent. HD equal to your caster level: deafened. HD up to caster level -1: staggered and deafened. HD up to caster level -5: paralyzed, staggered and deafened. HD up to caster level -10: killed, paralyzed, staggered and deafened. Deafened lasts 1d4 rounds and a save negates it; staggered lasts 2d4 rounds, reduced to 1d4 by a save; paralyzed and helpless lasts 1d10 minutes, reduced to 1 round by a save; killed slays living creatures and destroys undead, and a save reduces it to 3d6 points of damage plus 1 per caster level, maximum +25. One save covers every effect a creature suffers. Creatures with more Hit Dice than your caster level are unaffected entirely. Cast on your home plane, it also banishes nonlawful extraplanar creatures in the area to their own planes for at least 24 hours whether they heard it or not, negated by a Will save at a -4 penalty.

dictum.notes: The 3d6 + 1/level is deliberately NOT a damage spec. It only applies to creatures in the lowest Hit Dice band - those at least 10 HD below your caster level - and only when they SUCCEED at the save; every other creature that saves takes no damage at all. A damage spec on on_success would hit every creature in the spread that made its save. The four HD bands cannot be expressed in the vocabulary at all.

die-for-your-master.notes: The permission belongs to the spell's target - the animal companion, eidolon, familiar or mount - not to the caster. It functions as bleed for your master, broadened to attacks that need no attack roll.

effects.target: A green ray, requiring a ranged touch attack, covers the creature or object struck in a shimmering emerald field that completely blocks extradimensional travel: astral projection, blink, dimension door, ethereal jaunt, etherealness, gate, maze, plane shift, shadow walk, teleport and similar spell-like abilities, along with the use of a gate or teleportation circle. It does not disturb creatures already ethereal or astral when it is cast, does not block extradimensional perception or attack forms, and does not stop summoned creatures vanishing when their summoning ends.

dimensional-anchor.notes: A prohibition on a class of movement, which the vocabulary has no type for - immunity is about being harmed, not about being barred.

dimensional-blade.notes: Duration is a flat 1 round, not per level.

effects.target: teleport as a swift action from where you stand to either of two locations you designated at casting, as though by dimension door, carrying willing creatures and objects you touch

dimensional-bounce.notes: Corpus duration is '1 round/level or until discharged'. The format has an until_discharged kind but not both at once, so the timed duration is emitted and the charge limit is in the narrative.

Two versions. Prune Growth shrinks normal vegetation within long range to about a third its size, untangled and neatly trimmed, and automatically dispels plant-enhancing effects such as entangle, plant growth and wall of thorns; the area may be a 100-foot-radius circle, a 150-foot-radius semicircle or a 200-foot-radius quarter-circle, and you may exempt parts of it. Stunt Growth instead halves the coming year's productivity of all normal plants within half a mile. Neither version affects plant creatures.

diminish-resistance.notes: Not emitted as a resistance spec with a negative amount, for two reasons. The energy type is chosen by the caster at casting and never fixed by the spell, so no damage_type could be named without inventing one; and subtracting from an existing resistance with a floor of 0 is not the same thing as granting resistance -5, which an engine could read as vulnerability.

effects.target: Whenever you would fall inside the area of a detection spell such as detect magic, detect evil or detect undead, that area counts as half its size for the purpose of detecting you or your possessions. The detecting caster never learns her range was cut - you simply do not register.

diminished-detection.notes: Alters another spell's area rather than doing anything to a creature, which the vocabulary has no type for.

effects.target: Each round you concentrate on one target within range and know whether it deliberately and knowingly speaks a lie, read from the disturbances lying makes in its aura. discern-lies.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 round per caster level. A target's Will save keeps its own lies hidden; it does not stop the spell, so no save_gate is emitted.

effects.target: You learn the exact location of one creature or object: the name of the place, business or building, the community, the county or equivalent, the country, the continent and the plane. It goes straight through the usual protections against scrying and location, and nothing short of mind blank or a deity's direct intervention stops it. To find a creature you must have seen it or hold something that once belonged to it; to find an object you must have touched it at least once.

You scan one creature's thoughts and learn the names and locations of its living relatives, along with how the target feels about each of them and how they feel about the target - one relative for each round you concentrate. Because it reads the target's mind, you learn only what the target itself knows or believes.

discern-next-of-kin.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

effects.target: Analyses what objects are worth to an average trader. You name a minimum value at casting - 1 gp, 100 gp, 1,000 gp or whatever you like. First round: whether anything in range is worth at least that much. Second round: the single most valuable object in range glows brighter than the rest, direction only outside line of sight. Third round: everything within 10% of that top value glows faintly too. It says nothing about magical properties and does not register artifacts or priceless items.

discern-value.notes: Concentration up to a maximum of 1 minute per caster level.

disfiguring-touch.notes: The caster picks one penalty from a menu at casting, and the ability score, the attack-or-saves choice, and the speed option are all left open. effects.target: Armour Class against attacks by chaotic neutral, lawful neutral, neutral evil and neutral good creatures
Armour Class against attacks by creatures whose alignment is neutral with no other component

On a successful melee touch attack against a creature from another plane with a neutral component to its alignment, you may banish it to its home plane; its spell resistance applies and a Will save negates, at a -2 penalty if it is neutral with no other component. This use discharges the spell. Separately, with a touch you can automatically dispel any one enchantment cast by a creature with a neutral component to its alignment, with no save and no spell resistance, and this too discharges the spell. dispel-balance.notes: Both AC bonuses are situational_mod rather than combat_mod because each applies only against attackers of particular alignments, and the two never apply at once - a plain +3 or +5 to AC would hold against every attack in the game. The spell ends the moment either the banishment or the dispel is used.
